items.title: A Teen Rescuer Helped Save a Lost Senior Hiker with FaceTime Tech Support
items.summary:
A 17-year-old search-and-rescue volunteer helped locate a lost 88-year-old hiker in Northern California after conventional cellphone-tracking methods failed.

The volunteer rescuer, named Cody Davis, eventually used FaceTime to take control of the hiker’s iPhone screen and retrieve her GPS coordinates.

“I’m not a super tech person,” Davis told Outside. “But I’m young, and it’s easy for us to figure stuff like that out.”

The woman was found uninjured on November 10 at Mount Burdell Preserve, near Novato, California, after becoming separated from her hiking companions. Molly Williams, operations director for Marin County Search and Rescue, told Outside that the woman had gotten off the trail and headed downhill, although it remains unclear how the separation happened. Her companions tried unsuccessfully to locate her before calling for help.

Around 50 members of Marin County Search and Rescue mobilized to search the preserve. Williams, who oversaw the operation, said rescuers received the call around 2 P.M. and located the woman around 4 P.M.

When Rescue Tech Failed, a Teenager Took Over the Screen 
 A report of the rescue mission was published on the Marin County Search and Rescue group’s Facebook page.

Davis, a high school senior, was among the first search and rescue volunteers to arrive on the scene. According to Williams, Marin County’s search-and-rescue team accepts volunteers as young as 14.

“Probably a third or more of our members are high school age, and they are full members,” Williams said. “They respond in the same ways as the adults.”

Before rescuers…
items.t: A Teen Rescuer Helped Save a Lost Senior Hiker with FaceTime Tech Support

items.title: The Ephemeral Global Climbing School Amid China’s Epic Limestone
items.summary:
On October 22, hundreds of climbers of all skill levels descended upon Yangshuo, China, for the long-awaited  2026 Arc’teryx Climb Academy. Participants say the remarkable thing about the weekend wasn’t just the climbing or even the new skills they learned—it was the magic of the remote, fantastical landscape, and the opportunity to connect with people across cultures and continents.

The Arc’teryx Climb Academy is a roving international climbing school—and one that offers some of the most advanced mountain education in the world. Since 2007, academies have been held in global climbing epicenters like Squamish, Chamonix, and Mammoth Lakes. Some focus on climbing while others offer backcountry or freeride skiing education. Each installment is a complex undertaking, bringing together world-class guides and athletes to pass on their knowledge in a highly efficient, structured format. Dozens of courses—ranging from alpine overnights to big wall workshops to mental resilience clinics—are designed to meet participants where they’re at. At each academy, students can learn skills from scratch, drill fundamentals, or significantly boost their skills, even within just a few days of instruction.

(Photo: Arc’teryx) 
 While there are tons of events in the climbing universe, Arc’teryx Climb Academies stand out for just how seamlessly they’re run and how well integrated they are into the local community. items.title: Rescuers Carried a 105-Pound Labrador down a Steep Virginia Mountain after Two Days
items.summary:
When Roanoke County’s technical rescue teams were called to a steep Virginia mountainside on November 11, the stranded subject wasn’t a hiker or climber. It was Archie, a 105-pound yellow Labrador Retriever who had been missing for two days.

The nine-year-old dog disappeared on November 9 while his owner was hiking in the Bent Mountain area, according to Facebook updates from Angels of Assisi , a Roanoke animal welfare organization. After searchers located the dog by following his howls, firefighters from three stations helped carry Archie down the mountainside in a specialized rescue stretcher.

An Uphill Battle 
 Basit Jimoh, lead surgical assistant at Angels of Assisi, told Outside he joined the search on November 10 after learning that Archie was missing. According to Jimoh, searchers deployed drones in the area that evening, hoping to spot Archie from above, but turned up nothing.

The following afternoon, officials received reports from people hearing a dog whining on the steep, wooded mountainside. With the leaf-covered slope too slick to descend safely from above, Jimoh approached from the bottom, calling Archie’s name and listening for his howls to guide him uphill.

“I had a horse-leading halter and wrapped that around myself,” Jimoh said. “I started climbing, and whenever there was a tree close by, I’d wrap it around the tree and use it to pull myself up.”

Eventually, Jimoh found Archie lying in a ditch beneath a fallen tree.

“When he first saw somebody after being stuck in that ditch for two days, he was really excited,” Jimoh said. “He was wagging his tail.…
items.t: Rescuers Carried a 105-Pound Labrador down a Steep Virginia Mountain after Two Days

items.title: The Historic SS United States Was Sunk off Florida to Become the World’s Largest Artificial Reef
items.summary:
As it turns out, it takes a lot to sink a 990-foot ocean liner.

The SS United States was supposed to start going down at 1 p.m. Central Time on Wednesday, November 11. Last-minute preparations pushed that to nearly 5 p.m. By 4:45, every valve was open, and the Gulf was pouring in. Then came four more hours of watching a ship refuse to leave. She finally slipped under at 8:59 P.M., twenty-two nautical miles southwest of Destin, Florida, in the Gulf of Mexico, tilting hard to her port side.

From a nearby boat, I watched the fastest ocean liner ever built make the slowest exit imaginable. On her maiden voyage in 1952, she beat the Queen Mary ’s record by about ten hours . On Veterans Day, the iconic ocean liner needed about four hours just to go under.

With this scuttling—a deliberate, controlled sinking—the SS United States becomes the world’s largest artificial reef , surpassing the USS Oriskany , which had held the title since its 2006 sinking . It’s a second life that’s part habitat project and part tourism bet, and it follows years of failed rescue plans and a last-minute court fight.

SS United States before sinking off Florida coast. (Photo: Nick Tomecek / Destin-Fort Walton Beach) 
 Here’s how a ship once meant to become a museum ended up on the Gulf floor, what it means for the sea around her, and what divers can expect when they finally get to explore her underwater.

items.title: Great Hydration is About More than Just Electrolytes
items.summary:
Hydration comes up a lot when we talk about performance and recovery. Are you drinking enough water? Are you getting enough electrolytes? Are you tracking your fluid intake? It can be overwhelming to keep tabs of every statistic and ounce, but the hype around hydration isn’t without cause. Hydration is not only an essential component of pre-, mid- and post-workout performance. It’s an essential part of everyday life.

The Importance of Electrolytes 
 Electrolytes are a particular point of focus among performance athletes. Electrolytes are the minerals that help maintain the balance of fluids inside and outside your body’s cells. This is a critical consideration when it comes to high-exertion workouts where you’re losing lots of fluids through sweat.

The market is more saturated (pun intended) than ever with tablets, powders and pouches galore to help you optimize and maximize your electrolyte intake. But hydration doesn’t have to be as complicated as all that—and the conversation surrounding electrolytes doesn’t have to be reserved for elite athletes. It can be an everyday consideration for your morning walk, a quick out-and-back hike, or your daily commute to the office. And it all starts with a single coconut.

That’s the mission behind Harmless Harvest , a California-based company championing the coconut, turning a remarkable fruit into a remarkable lineup of products. items.t: Great Hydration is About More than Just Electrolytes
